Common concerns

Accounting risks can quietly arise at any stage

From incorporation to expansion, these four issues can quietly affect your cash flow and legal security.

An accounting foundation flawed from day one

A system built only to satisfy tax authorities can create poor data from the outset, exposing founders to billions of dong in penalties or costly rebuilding when the business expands.

Managing blindly without management data

Without a forward-looking dashboard, leaders may rely on intuition rather than sound source data when deciding to cut losses, allocate capital or set prices.

The risk burden of an in-house accounting team

An in-house accounting team carries fixed costs and substantial risk; delays, errors and legal pitfalls can remain hidden without qualified oversight.

Legacy books can hide a ticking time bomb

Fictitious balances, unsupported costs and inventory discrepancies can surface just as a business faces a tax inspection, fundraising or merger negotiations.

Current business context

Accounting and tax are now vital to business survival and competitiveness

Compliance pressure, staff capability requirements, investor expectations of transparency and outsourcing trends are reshaping accounting operations in Vietnam.

Accounting and tax compliance is essential to business survival

Even a small bookkeeping or tax-filing error can lead to additional tax, penalties or suspension of operations, directly affecting business survival.

Evolving, increasingly complex accounting and tax rules require highly skilled staff

Frequent accounting and tax updates are difficult for internal teams to keep pace with without specialist expertise and ongoing learning.

Investors, banks and funding partners expect stronger corporate governance

Unstandardized financial records or weak governance can limit access to capital or result in a valuation below a business's true worth.

Internal controls and accounting oversight requirements are increasing

Without independent controls, an accounting function may conceal prolonged errors or fraud that is not detected in time.

Accounting and payroll outsourcing has become a lasting mainstream trend

Clear accountability and operational efficiency are leading more businesses to outsource rather than maintain in-house teams.

Beyond compliance, management accounting is becoming a key competitive tool

Financial accounting meets regulatory obligations, while strong management data enables faster, more accurate decisions than industry peers.

Do not let accounting risks become a ticking time bomb

6 core services

Crown Accounting solutions for every business stage

Six services address key needs: building foundations, supporting management, adding capacity and standardizing existing systems.

Accounting foundations

Accounting system setup for newly invested businesses

Set up accounts, reference codes, supporting documents and posting procedures from the outset to create a foundation for compliance and management.

BenefitsReduce input errors and the need to reorganize systems as the business expands.
Discuss this service
Management accounting

Management accounting system development

Develop management reports and analyze costs, break-even points and profitability by product, department or relevant management unit.

BenefitsProvide data to assess performance, adjust prices, allocate resources and plan business activities.
Discuss this service
Full-service outsourcing

Outsourced accounting and payroll for businesses or projects

Handle accounting, invoicing, payroll and insurance within the agreed scope, with organized data handover, transaction processing and periodic reporting.

BenefitsAdapt accounting resources to demand and clarify shared responsibilities so the business can focus on operations.
Discuss this service
Outsourced controller

Outsourced financial controller and chief accountant

Assign senior personnel as financial controller or chief accountant to review transactions, organize closing and prepare and sign reports within their assigned roles.

BenefitsStrengthen professional oversight, improve error controls and reduce the risk of losses during operations.
Discuss this service
Competency assessment

Accounting competency assessment and standardization

Assess accounting knowledge, transaction-handling skills and regulatory awareness, identify competency gaps and recommend standardization measures.

BenefitsProvide a basis for work allocation, training and team development aligned with business management needs.
Discuss this service
Special services

Accounting system standardization for operating businesses

Review books, receivables and payables, expenses and inventory; reconcile data and identify discrepancies and tax risks to develop corrective actions.

BenefitsClarify unresolved balances and strengthen record reliability before explanations, fundraising or transactions.

Special service — recurring subscription

Crown Support Intelligence (CSI) — View your books through a tax authority's lens

For businesses with in-house accounting teams seeking an additional layer of independent review and ongoing risk alerts before problems arise.

Principle: An expert reference resource, never a substitute for day-to-day execution. CSI is a direct line to Crown's tax and accounting experts, not an outsourced accounting department.
Subscribe to Crown Support Intelligence (CSI)

  • Continuous review and risk alerts

    Proactively review business-provided reporting data and flag potential tax risks from the tax authority's perspective.

  • Risk assessment modeled on tax authority review logic

    Crown Accounting develops software that models tax authority risk reviews, analyzing business-provided data to detect risks before the authority does.

  • Understanding new tax rules

    Explain newly issued tax circulars and decrees with practical application guidance so internal teams can apply them correctly from the start.

  • Multidimensional, reliable and effective information

    Connect to a proprietary information network providing early warnings on tax, accounting and financial risks.
